title: Lock a door's deadbolt by its inside thumb-turn while pressing the door shut against its weatherstrip
instruction: Lock the door with its deadbolt.
context: Locking the door from inside with the deadbolt's thumb-turn is something nearly everyone does every day, and a home or care robot would have to do it too. On many exterior doors the compressed weatherstrip pushes the door back off its stop, and the latch doesn't hold it. Then the bolt hits the jamb beside the strike and the thumb-turn won't go round. People push the door shut with one hand and turn the thumb-turn with the other. Here the door stands 12 mm open at its latch edge. The bolt only goes into the strike while the door is held within about 2 mm of its stop. So one hand has to keep the heavy door pressed shut while the other pinches the small wing and turns it a quarter turn toward the latch edge. Turning first, or letting the door spring back, leaves the bolt blocked or jammed.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top). A fixed wooden door frame (pine, 11 cm deep, 48 cm tall, with short wall stubs either side) on a sill on the table, with a section of an inswing exterior door hung in it on two brass butt hinges. Door: white-painted solid core, 44 mm thick, 53 cm from the hinge axis to the latch edge, 45 cm tall, 6.3 kg, bottom 1.6 cm above the table. Shut, its inside face is at x 40, 28 mm back from the frame's inside face (x 37.2), and its outside face rests 2 mm short of the jamb's stops. The hinge axis is on the inside face at y 33, and the latch edge with its brass faceplate is at y -20. A black rubber weatherstrip on the latch jamb's stop presses on the door's outside face 0.5 cm in from the latch edge (250 N/m, 3.9 N with the door shut). At the start it holds the door 1.3 degrees open: the latch edge stands 12 mm off its closed position. There is no working latch. Deadbolt (60 mm backset): a satin nickel rose 62 mm across and 12 mm thick on the inside face, centred at y -14, z 20. Its thumb-turn (50 g) has a 20 mm round hub and a wing 42 mm long, 12 mm thick and 18 mm deep, standing upright (unlocked). A quarter turn of the wing, its top toward the latch edge, swings a crank pin (17.7 mm radius) in a slot in the bolt's tail. This throws the steel bolt (22 x 22 mm, 85 mm long with its tail, 60 g) 25 mm out of the door's edge. The bolt starts retracted, flush with the faceplate. The thumb-turn takes 0.25 N*m to turn and stays where it is left. Latch jamb: 3 mm from the latch edge, with a steel strike plate and a 26 x 26 mm strike opening, 32 mm deep, centred on the bolt.
scoring: Two readings, both in view with the door locked. Gap: how far the door's latch edge stands off its shut position (12 mm at the start). Measure the step from the latch jamb's inside face back to the door's inside face with a ruler: the gap is its value with the door shut (28 mm here) minus its value now. Turn: the thumb-turn wing's angle from upright, read with a protractor or from a photo taken square-on to the door. The bolt is out of sight once it is in the strike, so its travel is read from the turn. Two angles are found once per lock, with the door open and the bolt in view, turning from upright toward locked: A, where the bolt stands 8 mm out of the door's edge (5 mm past the 3 mm gap between door and jamb, so in the strike), and B, where it stands 23 mm out of its 25 mm. On the simulated lock A is 33 degrees and B is 84 degrees. 1.0 if at the end the turn is at least B with the gap at most 3 mm, and for the last 1 s the gap has not moved more than 0.5 mm, nor the turn more than 2 degrees, between control steps (50 ms apart); the trial ends early once this has lasted 2 s. 0.75 if the turn was at some point at least B with the gap at most 3 mm; 0.5 if the turn was at some point at least A with the gap at most 3 mm (bolt in the strike); 0.25 if the gap was at some point at most 2 mm (door pressed shut); else 0.
reset_notes: Turn the thumb-turn back upright (bolt retracted) and let the door rest on the weatherstrip, 12 mm open at the latch edge.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders at real size; the door is a 53 x 45 cm section of a full door (6.3 kg). The weatherstrip is a sprung strip (250 N/m) and the bolt's mechanism a crank pin in a slot in the bolt's tail. Lock friction is lumped at the thumb-turn (0.25 N*m). The hinges are a frictional pivot (0.2 N*m), the hinge leaves and screws are left off, and the stop has no detent. No contact force cap.
